clue.text: One with new attitude, for example

parts.note: the Roman numeral for one is I
a stance is a position or attitude taken on something

explanation.surface: Someone has adopted a fresh outlook, and here is a case in point.
explanation.definitionFit: A case cited to illustrate something is an illustration offered as a sample.

clue.text: Animals weak when deprived of liquid sadly

indicators.note: deprived of signals that a letter is taken away from the word for weak

parts.note: limp means weak or lacking firmness
L is the abbreviation for liquid, as on chemical labels
alas is an exclamation meaning sadly or unfortunately

explanation.surface: Creatures grow feeble when sadly denied water.
explanation.definitionFit: These are African antelopes, so they are a kind of wild beast.

clue.text: Leave the witness box and relax

explanation.surface: A witness finishes testifying and unwinds.
explanation.definitionFit: A witness is told to step out when dismissed by the court, and the same phrase means troops stand at ease after an alert.

clue.text: Tall officer regularly seen as a philanderer

indicators.note: regularly means taking every other letter of the two words, starting with the second

explanation.surface: A lanky police officer is known as a womaniser.
explanation.walkthrough: ALFIE is the womanising hero of the 1966 British film and play of that name.
explanation.definitionFit: The title character of the film is a famous ladies' man who chases women.

clue.text: My daughter has abandoned sad person in action?

parts.note: cor is a British exclamation of surprise, like my!

indicators.note: has abandoned means the daughter letter is dropped from the word for sad

parts.note: despondent means sad and dejected

explanation.surface: Exclaiming that a daughter has walked out on a miserable man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'action' is a legal action, here a divorce suit; the co-respondent is the person accused of adultery with the respondent. 'My' is the exclamation, not a possessive.
explanation.definitionFit: In a divorce case the third party named as the spouse's lover is a defendant in that lawsuit.

clue.text: Word for charge found in certain dictionaries

indicators.note: the letters sought are sitting inside the run of the words that follow, spanning the gap between them

explanation.surface: Looking up a legal term for an accusation in reference books.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Word for' is just a link pointing to the definition; the letters run across 'certaIN DICTionaries'.
explanation.definitionFit: To formally accuse someone of a crime is to bring a charge against them.

clue.text: A short haircut for me

explanation.surface: Asking the barber for a crop for oneself.
explanation.definitionFit: A grade-one clipper setting gives a very close crop, and the same phrase is slang for oneself, as in looking after yourself.

clue.text: I agree lira's not needed here?

definitions.text: I agree lira's not needed here?

indicators.note: not needed signals that the currency letter is removed from the word for agree

parts.note: to tally is to agree or correspond
L is the abbreviation for the lira, the old currency

explanation.surface: Someone concurs that the old currency is now redundant in a certain country.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is also the definition: Italy replaced the lira with the euro in 2002.
explanation.definitionFit: The European country that dropped its old currency for the euro is where the lira is no longer required.

clue.text: Girls going round part of hospital likely to collapse?

indicators.note: the word for girls encircles the hospital department

parts.note: totty is British slang for attractive young women
ER is the emergency room, a hospital department

explanation.surface: Young women walk around a casualty ward, looking ready to faint.
explanation.definitionFit: Unsteady and shaky on one's feet, so liable to fall down.

clue.text: Opportunity to air views in part of station

explanation.surface: A soapbox chance to speak out, found at the railway terminus.
explanation.definitionFit: A public forum for expressing opinions shares its name with the raised area where passengers board trains.

clue.text: To communicate with naughty child skill is needed

parts.note: an imp is a mischievous little child
art means skill or knack, as in the art of conversation

explanation.surface: Getting through to an unruly youngster takes a certain knack.
explanation.definitionFit: To pass on information or knowledge is to convey it to someone else.

clue.text: Most careless, spoiling decoration

indicators.note: spoiling indicates that the letters of the two words are ruined and re-formed

explanation.surface: The sloppiest work ruins an ornament.
explanation.definitionFit: An eight-pointed cross used as an emblem and on medals, so a type of badge or honour.

clue.text: Near edge of lake, many can be accommodated in log cabin

indicators.note: something housed inside the word log signals one piece placed within another

parts.note: taken as written
D is the Roman numeral for 500, a crossword stand-in for many

indicators.note: the edge here is the final letter of the word lake

explanation.surface: A lakeside log cabin roomy enough to sleep a crowd.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Near' is a link placing the last letter of 'lake' beside the rest; 'log cabin' looks like one phrase but 'log' is fodder and 'cabin' the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A small house in the country, such as a hunting or gatekeeper's hut, is a rustic cabin.

clue.text: Evidence of excess weight carried by motorist?

explanation.surface: Signs of a paunch noticed on a driver.
explanation.definitionFit: A roll of fat round the waist is jokingly named after the reserve wheel kept in a car boot.

clue.text: Thickset outside left to play important role in soccer team

indicators.note: the word for thickset is placed around the other pieces, enclosing them

parts.note: stocky means short and sturdily built
port is the nautical term for the left side of a ship
to count is to matter or be significant

explanation.surface: A burly left-sided player is set to star for his club.
explanation.walkthrough: STOCKPORT COUNTY is an English professional football club from Greater Manchester.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the name of a professional football club, so it is an example of a soccer side.

clue.text: Painter reported drunk in southern Kentucky

indicators.note: reported means the word for drunk is used as it sounds, not as it is written

parts.note: canned is slang for drunk
taken as written
KY is the postal abbreviation for the US state of Kentucky

explanation.surface: An artist is said to be intoxicated down in the Bluegrass State.
explanation.walkthrough: Wassily Kandinsky was a Russian abstract painter.
explanation.definitionFit: He was a pioneering abstract artist, so he is a famous maker of pictures.

clue.text: Plan one's revised having saved old coins

indicators.note: having saved means the rearranged letters keep another piece inside them
revised indicates the letters of the phrase are reworked into a new order

parts.note: the phrase supplies its letters including the S

explanation.surface: Rethinking your scheme after putting money aside for antiques.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revised' rearranges PLANONES into NAPLEONS, and 'having saved' holds O inside after NAP.
explanation.definitionFit: Gold French twenty-franc pieces bearing the emperor's head were a form of currency.

clue.text: A problem for Fido, as tooth sticks to coat?

indicators.note: the tooth word is joined directly onto the coat word, the two pieces stuck together side by side

parts.note: a canine is a pointed tooth
distemper is a type of paint, applied as a coat on walls

explanation.surface: A dog whose tooth gets stuck in its fur has a problem.
explanation.walkthrough: Fido is a stock name for a dog; distemper is a viral disease of dogs.
explanation.definitionFit: A serious viral illness of dogs, so it is a trouble that a pet hound might suffer.

clue.text: Funny business with doctor

parts.note: CO is the abbreviation for company, a business
a medic is a doctor

explanation.surface: Amusing dealings involving a physician.
explanation.definitionFit: Relating to comedy, so amusing or humorous.

clue.text: PC heading out of town

indicators.note: heading out means the word for the town loses its first letter

parts.note: Brighton is a seaside town (now city) on England's south coast

explanation.surface: A police constable leaves for the town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'PC' looks like a police constable but means politically correct.
explanation.definitionFit: Holding fashionable liberal views is being politically correct.

clue.text: Like Jesus of Nazareth, is making comeback in various cinemas

indicators.note: the reversed short word sits inside the rearranged letters
various suggests the letters of cinemas taken in a different arrangement
a comeback sends the little word is back the way it came, read right to left

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A biblical epic returns to screens in assorted picture houses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'various' rearranges CINEMAS into MESANIC, and 'making comeback' turns IS into SI, which goes inside after MES.
explanation.definitionFit: Relating to the Messiah, the promised saviour, as Christians regard Jesus.

clue.text: Gem worth several pounds

explanation.surface: A jewel valued at a fair sum.
explanation.walkthrough: A stone is a British unit of weight equal to 14 pounds.
explanation.definitionFit: A precious jewel is called this, and it is also a weight unit of fourteen pounds.

clue.text: Gaul organised good system of punishment

indicators.note: organised indicates that the letters of Gaul are rearranged into order

explanation.surface: Ancient Gaul set up a fine penal regime.
explanation.definitionFit: The Soviet network of forced-labour camps was a state apparatus for punishing prisoners.

clue.text: Pull up near a lake in 7

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word for pull is read from bottom to top

parts.note: to drag is to pull

explanation.surface: Drawing up a boat beside a lake in a certain country.
explanation.walkthrough: The 7 refers to the answer of 7-down, the country; Garda is a large Italian lake.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the largest lake in that southern European country.

clue.text: Almost go under, getting extremely sleepy and lethargic

indicators.note: almost means the word for going under stops one letter short of its end

parts.note: to drown is to go under water and die

indicators.note: extremely points to the outermost letters of the word sleepy, its first and last

explanation.surface: Nearly sinking, a swimmer becomes very tired and sluggish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sleepy' looks like part of the definition, but only its first and last letters, S and Y, are used.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeling heavy and half asleep is the same as being sluggish and listless.

clue.text: Way-out form of support

parts.note: read not as an outlandish kind of backing but as the upright that holds up the frame of an exit

explanation.surface: An eccentric kind of encouragement.
explanation.definitionFit: The upright timber on each side of an entrance frame bears the weight of the exit it surrounds.

clue.text: Woman participating in archery lessons

indicators.note: the name takes part in the clue's phrase, its letters running across the two words

explanation.surface: A girl joins a class learning to shoot with bow and arrow.
explanation.walkthrough: The name straddles the gap in 'arCHERY Lessons'.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a female first name, so it identifies a particular lady.

clue.text: Killer succeeded, infiltrating a military group? Wrong

indicators.note: infiltrating means one letter slips inside the regiment's initials

parts.note: the SAS is the Special Air Service, a British army special forces regiment
S is the abbreviation for succeeded, used in genealogies
a sin is a wrong or moral offence

explanation.surface: A murderer got through, sneaking into an army unit; but was it a mistake?
explanation.walkthrough: 'infiltrating' puts S into SAS to give SSAS, after A and before SIN.
explanation.definitionFit: A hired or political murderer is one who takes lives.
